server.instructions: Hypora platform tools for one run. Typical order: inspect_dataset -> write_trial_files -> submit_experiment -> get_experiment_status (poll until finished) -> get_experiment_metrics, or get_experiment_logs to diagnose a failure. The platform owns the data split, the held-out labels, and every metric. No tool returns raw dataset rows.
server.name: hypora

tools.description:
Summarize an authorized tabular dataset without revealing any of its rows.

Use it first, to learn the dataset's shape before designing a trial: column types,
missing values, value ranges, the target's class balance, ID-like columns, candidate
group keys (repeated subjects or batches), timestamps, and leakage candidates (single
columns that predict the target suspiciously well; a signal to review, not proof).

Do not use it to look at rows, samples, or individual values: no tool returns them (the
data firewall). Categorical columns list at most their five most frequent labels.

Returns a DatasetProfile. `tabular.leakage_screen_skipped_reason`, when set, means
leakage was not screened; an empty `leakage_candidates` list then proves nothing.
Profiles are cached: repeating the same call is cheap.

Example: inspect_dataset(dataset_id="ds_main")

dataset_id.description: An authorized dataset ID, e.g. 'ds_main'. Omit for the dataset the run's experiment contract governs.
dataset_id.title: Dataset Id

target.description: Column to treat as the label for target-aware statistics. Omit to use the contract's target (or, before a contract exists, no target).
target.title: Target

task_type.description: Required with `target`: binary/multiclass classification or regression.

tools.name: inspect_dataset

FeatureAssociation.description:
Single-feature association with the target, for any feature (spec §5.2 "per-feature
target-association statistics"). Flagged ones are also listed as LeakageCandidate.
FeatureAssociation.title: FeatureAssociation

GroupKeyCandidate.description: A column whose rows share targets more than chance (spec §5.2, PLAN.md S1.1).

chance_level.description: The same statistic under random grouping.
chance_level.title: Chance Level

GroupKeyCandidate.title: GroupKeyCandidate

LeakageCandidate.description: A feature that alone predicts the target suspiciously well (a candidate, not a verdict).
LeakageCandidate.title: LeakageCandidate

MetricName.description: Metrics computed by platform code (spec §18; PLAN.md S1.3).
MetricName.title: MetricName

NumericSummary.description: Distribution summary of a numeric column (data-firewall safe: no rows).
NumericSummary.title: NumericSummary

leakage_screen_skipped_reason.description: Why leakage CV was skipped; null alone does not prove screening occurred.
leakage_screen_skipped_reason.title: Leakage Screen Skipped Reason

statistics_sample_size.description: Seeded sample rows used for expensive statistics; null for older profiles.
statistics_sample_size.title: Statistics Sample Size

outputSchema.description: Deterministic dataset summary (spec §5.2 stage 2). Summaries only, never raw rows.
outputSchema.title: DatasetProfile

tools.title: Profile a dataset

tools.description:
Create a trial, or replace its files, in the run's own trial directory.

A trial tests ONE hypothesis. Its pipeline.py is model code that the platform runs in a
sandbox: `fit(train, ctx)` receives `train.X` / `train.y` (pandas; training rows only)
and must do all learned preprocessing (imputation, scaling, encoding) inside fit;
`predict(model, X)` returns `runtime.Predictions(values, probabilities, classes)`, with
class probabilities in sorted-label order for classification. Import `Predictions` from
`runtime`. The platform, never this code, splits the data and computes the metrics.

Use it to start a trial (omit trial_id), or to fix a trial after reading its logs
(pass trial_id and only the files that change). Then call submit_experiment.

Do not use it to read files or to write anywhere but this trial: paths are fixed. Do not
print data from pipeline.py; output that shows dataset values is withheld from logs.

Returns the trial_id, the files written (SHA-256, size), the files the trial now has,
and `submit_defaults`: the values submit_experiment uses for omitted arguments.

Example: write_trial_files(idempotency_key="run_104:wr_0001", design={"kind":
"baseline", "operation": "fit", "hypothesis": "A majority-class predictor sets the
floor", "model_family": "dummy", "expected_effect": "f1_macro near 0.4",
"estimated_cost": {"compute_seconds": 30}}, pipeline_py="...")

CostEstimate.description: Estimated cost of running something (`estimate_experiment`, spec §8.3).
CostEstimate.title: CostEstimate

ShortBudget.description: Reduced budget for a successive-halving round (spec §8.4).
ShortBudget.title: ShortBudget

TrialDesign.description:
One hypothesis (spec §8.1 `trial.yaml`: hypothesis, model family, config, expected effect,
estimated cost), plus the operation and model it needs.
TrialDesign.title: TrialDesign

design.description: The trial's hypothesis and plan, saved as trial.yaml. Required when creating a trial. For a fit trial: kind 'baseline' or 'candidate', operation 'fit'.

idempotency_key.description: '{run_id}:{unique id}', e.g. 'run_104:wr_0001'. Use a NEW key for every new write; resend the SAME key only to retry a write whose reply you did not receive (it returns the original result and writes nothing again).
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

pipeline_py.description: Full source of pipeline.py, defining fit(train, ctx) -> model and predict(model, X) -> Predictions (see the tool description). Required when creating a trial. At most 1 MiB.
pipeline_py.title: Pipeline Py

requirements_lock.description: Optional requirements.lock: 'name==version' lines, each already installed in the sandbox image. New packages need user approval.
requirements_lock.title: Requirements Lock

trial_id.description: Omit to create a new trial; pass the trial_id from an earlier call to replace that trial's files, e.g. 'trl_4f2a9c1e'.
trial_id.title: Trial Id

tools.name: write_trial_files

SubmitDefaults.description: The values `submit_experiment` uses when its optional arguments are omitted.

limits.description: The contract's default (and maximum) job limits.

SubmitDefaults.title: SubmitDefaults

created.description: True if this call created the trial (a retry with the same idempotency_key returns this original result).
created.title: Created

submit_defaults.description: Null until the run has an approved experiment contract.

trial_dir.description: The trial's own directory, relative to the repository.
trial_dir.title: Trial Dir

trial_id.description: Pass this to write_trial_files and submit_experiment.
trial_id.title: Trial Id

tools.title: Write a trial's files

tools.description:
Queue one trial for platform-run validation; returns a job_id at once.

The platform freezes the trial's current files, then (in a sandbox, without network)
fits pipeline.py on each validation fold of the contract's split and scores the
predictions itself. Held-out test labels are never used here.

Use it after write_trial_files, and again after fixing a failed trial (with a NEW
idempotency_key). Then poll get_experiment_status until `finished` is true.

Do not use it to change the split, metric, features, or budget: they come from the
approved contract. Limits above the contract's are refused; only the user can extend
them.

Returns the job_id, its state (normally QUEUED), and whether the key was a duplicate.

Example: submit_experiment(trial_id="trl_4f2a9c1e", idempotency_key="run_104:sub_0001")

approval_ref.description: Omit to use the contract's approval; if given, it must match.
approval_ref.title: Approval Ref

config.description: Passed to fit/predict as ctx.config, e.g. {'max_depth': 6}.
config.title: Config

contract_version.description: Omit to use the current contract; if given, it must match.
contract_version.title: Contract Version

family.description: Only 'tabular' is supported in this version.

idempotency_key.description: '{run_id}:{unique id}', e.g. 'run_104:sub_0001'. Use a NEW key for every new submission; resend the SAME key only to retry a submission whose reply you did not receive.
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

limits.description: Sandbox limits per stage; omit for the contract's defaults. They can be lowered but never raised above the contract's defaults.

operation.description: Only 'fit' is supported in this version.

run_id.description: Omit; defaults to this session's run.
run_id.title: Run Id

trial_id.description: The trial to run, from write_trial_files.
trial_id.title: Trial Id

tools.name: submit_experiment

deduplicated.description: True if this idempotency_key was already used for this same submission: the existing job is returned and nothing new is queued.
deduplicated.title: Deduplicated

job_id.description: Pass this to the get_experiment_* tools.
job_id.title: Job Id

tools.title: Queue a trial for validation

tools.description:
Report where a submitted experiment is: queued, running, completed, or failed.

Use it to poll after submit_experiment (every few seconds) until `finished` is true;
then call get_experiment_metrics (if succeeded) or get_experiment_logs (if failed).

Do not use it for metrics (get_experiment_metrics) or full logs (get_experiment_logs).

Returns the job state, attempts, a platform-written error (code and message) if it
failed, the last log lines (lines that showed dataset values are withheld), the IDs of
stored artifacts, and the suggested next step.

Example: get_experiment_status(job_id="job_1761400000000000000_a1b2c3")
tools.name: get_experiment_status

message.description: Platform-written; dataset values are never included.
message.title: Message

finished.description: True once the state can no longer change.
finished.title: Finished

log_tail.description: Last log lines, after the data firewall.
log_tail.title: Log Tail

withheld_log_lines.description: Tail lines withheld because they showed dataset values.
withheld_log_lines.title: Withheld Log Lines

tools.title: Experiment status

tools.description:
Return the platform-computed validation scores of a completed experiment.

Every number is computed by platform code from the trial's saved predictions, never by
the trial itself. Use it once get_experiment_status reports `succeeded: true`, to compare
trials on the contract's primary metric and decide what to try next.

Do not use it before the job finishes (you get EXPERIMENT_NOT_FINISHED) or for test-set
scores: the held-out test split is scored only for a frozen final candidate.

Returns the primary metric and its direction, a mean/std/min/max summary of every metric
across folds, per-fold scores (with confusion matrices for classification), per-class
scores, and per-group spread for grouped splits (groups are unnamed: their labels are
data values).

Example: get_experiment_metrics(job_id="job_1761400000000000000_a1b2c3")
tools.name: get_experiment_metrics

index.description: The class's position in class_labels and in every confusion matrix.
index.title: Index

support.description: Validation rows of this class, all folds.
support.title: Support

confusion_matrix.description: Rows: true class; columns: predicted; both in class_labels order (index). Null for a fold whose classes differ from class_labels.
confusion_matrix.title: Confusion Matrix

unavailable.description: Why a metric is undefined on this fold.
unavailable.title: Unavailable

GroupSummary.description: Per-group scores of the primary metric, without group labels (they are data values).
GroupSummary.title: GroupSummary

MetricName.description: Metrics computed by platform code (spec §18; PLAN.md S1.3).
MetricName.title: MetricName

folds.description: Folds where the metric is defined.
folds.title: Folds

primary.description: Null if undefined on every fold.

tools.title: Experiment metrics

tools.description:
Read a submitted experiment's sandbox output (stdout and stderr), page by page.

Each sandbox stage (fit or predict, per validation fold) has its own log; lines are
numbered within their stage. Use it to diagnose a failed or surprising trial: Python
tracebacks, warnings, and training progress printed by pipeline.py.

Do not use it to read data: every line that shows dataset values is replaced by a
"withheld by the data firewall" marker, so printing rows from pipeline.py only hides
your own log lines.

Returns one page of lines (oldest first), the total line count, how many lines on this
page were withheld, and `next_page` (null on the last page).

Example: get_experiment_logs(job_id="job_1761400000000000000_a1b2c3", page=1)
tools.name: get_experiment_logs

line.description: Line number within the stage's log.
line.title: Line

withheld_lines.description: Lines on this page withheld because they showed dataset values.
withheld_lines.title: Withheld Lines
